txt:
Spend 1 Hope and make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 10 for civilian units, DC 15 for military units, or DC 20 for advanced AIs). On a success, take control of one Tier 1–2 mechanical unit within Close range for 1 hour. The unit follows your instructions within its normal technical capabilities.

On a Success with Hope, the duration extends to 4 hours and the unit may perform one action outside its standard parameters, at the Keeper's discretion.

On a failure, the attempt is detected. The unit's owner receives an unauthorized-access alert and the Keeper gains 1 Fear.

*This power cannot be used against a conscious Synthetic without that character's explicit consent.*

Spend 1 Hope and make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). On a success, touch a device or network and install an active cryptographic defense layer. Any attempt to hack that system must exceed the result of your Knowledge roll instead of the system's normal DC. The protection lasts until the end of the scene or for 1 hour, whichever is shorter.

On a Success with Hope, the system also alerts you silently whenever someone attempts access and reveals the attempt's point of origin.

On a failure, the protection fails and leaves a detectable signature. An Inspector with appropriate technical knowledge can identify the failed attempt with a Knowledge roll against DC 10.

Spend 1 Hope. Choose one electronic system within Close range. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 10/15/20 -Simple/Complex/Military). Success: You gain control of the system for 10 minutes, able to use its standard functions. On a Success with Hope: You can issue one simple, permanent command that the system will execute even after the duration ends (e.g., lock a door, send a message, activate an alarm).

Mark 1 Stress. Choose a security system you interacted with in the last hour. Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Success: You erase all records of your interaction within the last scene. On a Success with Hope: You can plant

subtle but convincing false evidence that points suspicion towards a rival individual or faction.
Mark 1 Stress. Touch a Drone, Vehicle, or Synthetic. The target recovers 1d8 + Knowledge HP. Efficiency: If the natural d8 result is 8, the Stress cost is refunded immediately.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You unleash a virus into a local network (1km radius) for 1 hour. Choose one effect: temporarily disable all security systems, cause all Tier 1-2 gear to malfunction on its next use, or copy a specific data set (requires a separate Knowledge check to sort). Failure: The system traces the virus, giving the Keeper Advantage on all rolls to track or identify you for 24 hours.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You fabricate simple, functional Tier 1 tech (tools, comms, weapons dealing (Proficiency)×d6 damage) in 10 minutes. The item lasts for one scene. On a Success with Hope: The creation is permanent and can be up to Tier 2 quality.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You partner your mind with an intelligent system (Tier 3-4 AI/ship computer) for one scene. You gain remote access to its functions and data, and Advantage on all Knowledge checks related to that system's domain. Failure: The AI rejects you, locking you out and treating you as a hostile entity for 1d6 rounds.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Over 1 hour, you can restore a permanently disabled ship system (e.g., from taking Hull Stress). The system functions normally for 24 hours. On a Success with Hope: The repair is permanent. This is a Long-Term Project if attempted during Downtime.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You permanently upgrade one allied piece of Tier 1-3 gear, granting it one Armor or Weapon Feature (e.g., \*Resilient\*, \*Flexible\*, \*Armor Piercing\*). The item cannot gain this benefit again. Failure: The gear suffers a temporary malfunction lasting until your next rest, and the owner Marks 1 Stress.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope. For one scene, you become the master of a star system's entire network infrastructure. You can monitor comms, control utility functions, and access public databases. Failure: You leave a massive digital footprint, automatically reducing your Reputation by 1 with the system's dominant faction.

Spend 2 Hope and mark 1 Stress, then make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). On a success, transfer your consciousness into a willing or inactive mind within Close range, such as a powered-down android, an unowned AI, or an unconscious body. The transfer lasts for no more than one scene.

**While transferred, you can:**

- Perceive through the host's senses.
- Communicate using the host's voice.
- Use Social and Neural Domain Powers as though you were physically present at the host's location.

**While transferred, you cannot:**

- Use Kinetic, Tech, or Synthesis Domain Powers, which require your physical body.
- Move beyond the host body's physical capabilities.
- Access the host's memories or technical abilities.

**Your physical body** remains unconscious and defenseless. Each time it takes damage during the transfer, mark 1 Stress. If your body is reduced to 0 HP, the transfer ends immediately and you enter the Dying state without the option to make a Death Move.

If the host dies or becomes incapacitated, the transfer ends and you mark 2 additional Stress when you return.

On a failure, the attempt destabilizes your mind. Gain a temporary Flaw—Disadvantage on one category of rolls chosen by the Keeper—until your next long rest, and mark 2 Stress.

*This power can never be used on another PC without that player's explicit consent.*

During Downtime, undertake the design and construction of a unique Tier 4 device, such as a prototype weapon, specialized augmentation, or experimental tool. Define its function, limitations, and potential side effects with the Keeper before beginning.

**Progress:** During each Downtime phase devoted to the project, make a Knowledge roll against DC 15. On a success, advance 1 segment. On a Success with Hope, advance 2 segments. On a failure, make no progress. On a Failure with Fear, make no progress and one current component is damaged, as determined by the Keeper.

**Completion:** Gain the device's schematic and a functional prototype. The prototype has the Experimental tag and begins with Degradation 1.

*At the start of any work phase, you may spend 1 Hope. If you do, the final prototype permanently retains the Experimental tag and takes twice as long to suffer its first Degradation.*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You and your crew undertake a Long-Term Project (6-clock) to fabricate one Tier 5 Starship Component (e.g., Reactor Core, Shield Emitter). Requires 3 Wealth Tier spent. On a Success with Hope: The component is masterfully built, granting +1 to the ship's Core Power allocation.

*Once per session*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope + 2 Stress. For one scene, target a ship or settlement in-system. Shut down its non-essential systems, OR disable one primary ship system (Weapons, Shields, Engines) for 1d4 rounds. Failure: Power surge. Your ship takes 2 Hull Stress OR your personal tech malfunctions for 1 hour.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 3 Hope + 2 Stress. Create a surge of technological acceleration in a 1 km radius for one scene. All allied gear up to Tier 3

gains Experimental Proficiency for the duration. Failure: The surge destabilizes nearby systems; the Keeper gains 3 Fear tokens, and all affected tech must make a Knowledge Reaction Roll (DC 15) or malfunction for the remainder of the scene.

Spend 5 Hope and mark 3 Stress, then make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 25). This action requires 10 uninterrupted minutes of preparation.

On a success, permanently transfer your consciousness into an appropriate Tier 5 AI form agreed upon with the Keeper. You gain a direct interface with any system in your current star system as a movement action, Experimental Proficiency with all Tech devices, and immunity to Physical damage while in digital form.

Your biological body enters dormancy. It does not die, but it cannot act and remains a point of physical vulnerability.

On a failure, the process fragments your consciousness. Lose access to one randomly determined Domain until you complete a personal mission lasting one story arc to restore it.

*This power requires the narrative consent of the entire table. The Keeper must discuss its campaign implications before resolving it.*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 30). You permanently awaken one Precursor Tier technology (e.g., a weapon, a derelict ship system) in a 1km radius. Cost: You Mark 4 Stress. Failure: The technology backfires, dealing 3 Hull Stress to your current location/ship.

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 3 Hope + 3 Stress. Establish a secure, instant communication network across three star systems for one scene. Allied characters on the network gain Advantage on all Knowledge rolls. Failure: The network's opening ping alerts all hostile entities in those systems to your location.

Mythic. Once per campaign. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 30). This is a Long-Term Project (12-clock) to construct one permanent Tier 5 Asset (e.g., orbital station, city dome). Cost: Requires 5 Hope and 5 Stress to begin. Failure: The project collapses, dealing 3d12 damage to you and permanently reducing your Knowledge Trait by 1.

Mythic. Once per campaign. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 30). You integrate one willing organic and one willing digital life form. The composite entity gains +2 to their highest Trait and can use both sets of Domain powers. Cost: Requires 5 Hope and 5 Stress. Failure: The integration is unstable. The caster suffers Disadvantage on all rolls for 1d6 days and the composite entity is dissolved.

Spend 1 Hope. Touch a living creature. You learn its current/max HP, and any active physical conditions. Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 10). Success: You also detect any diseases, toxins, or cybernetics.
Spend 1 Hope. You adapt your body to a hostile environment for one hour. You gain immunity to the harmful physical effects of vacuum, extreme temperature, toxicity, or ambient radiation.

Reaction (Cost: 1 Hope). When you or an ally in Very Close takes damage, the target recovers 1 HP immediately. Roll 1d4: the result is the number of additional turns the effect lasts. At the start of the target's turn, they recover +1 HP. Surge: If the natural d4 result is 4, the target also clears 1 Stress immediately.

Mark 1 Stress. You spend 10 minutes attuning to the local bio-environment (1km radius). For the next 24 hours, you gain Advantage on all Instinct rolls related to survival, navigation, or tracking within that area.

Mark 1 Stress. Choose a willing ally within Close range. For 1 hour, you share a telepathic link. Once during this time, when one of you spends Hope on a roll, the other gains Advantage on their next roll.

Cost: 1 Hope. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Create a 10m radius zone of perfect environment (breathable, safe temp, radiation-free) for 8 hours, benefiting up to 10 people. On a Success with Hope: The zone also provides basic, nourishing sustenance (equivalent to a Wealth Tier 1 Asset).

Cost: 1 Hope. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). For one scene, you bond your nervous system to the local biosphere's

dominant lifeform-type, your body briefly expressing one of its key adaptations. Choose one. On a Success with Hope: Choose a second. Apex Predator: Your unarmed strikes manifest claws, tusks, or fangs of the local predator stock, dealing (Proficiency)×d6 Void damage. You gain Resistance to Cold (your metabolism stabilizes against thermal stress). Aquatic Symbiote: You can breathe in any liquid medium and are not hindered by it; gills, vapor-membranes, or capillary skin manifest as needed. You gain Resistance to Fire (a thin sheen of moisture or temperature-regulating slime forms). Lithoderm: Bark, chitin, or mineralized scales harden across your skin. You gain 2 temporary Armor Slots and Resistance to Physical damage; your movement speed is halved. Sky-Adapted: Hollow bones, gas bladders, or photosynthetic membranes lift you into the air. You gain flight (hover) and +2 Evasion. You gain Resistance to Lightning (your form discharges electric potential through trailing filaments).

Cost: 1 Hope. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You rapidly evolve your form for one hour. Choose two adaptations: • \ *Natural Attack ((Proficiency)×d8 void)\* • \*Enhanced Senses (+2 Instinct)\* • \*Physical Adaptation (+1 Evasion)\ *

- \*Metabolic Change (remove 1 ongoing condition)\* On Success with Hope: The effect lasts for 24 hours or until you take a full rest.

Cost: 1 Hope. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You merge one piece of Tier 1-3 tech with yourself or a willing ally for 1 scene. You can interface with it by touch and heal it for 1d6 HP as an action. Failure: The target's body rejects the tech, dealing a direct 1 HP physical damage and 1 Stress.

Choose one mode when you activate this power:

**Focused Mode — Cost: 1 Hope.** Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). On a success, a creature you touch recovers Proficiency×d10 HP and clears 1 Stress. If the target is Dying, stabilize them before applying the healing.

On a Success with Hope, add Proficiency×d4 HP to the total healed.

**Distributed Mode — Cost: 2 Hope.** Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). On a success, affect up to three creatures within Close range. Each target recovers Proficiency×d6 HP.

On a Success with Hope, each target also clears 1 Stress.

On a failure in either mode, the power has no effect and the spent resources are not recovered.

Transform a 100-meter-radius area into an environment permanently habitable by Class IV humanoid life. Define the intended environment with the Keeper before beginning.

**Progress:** During each session actively devoted to the project, make a Knowledge roll against DC 15. On a success, advance 1 segment. On a Success with Hope, advance 2 segments and reduce that week's maintenance cost to 0. On a Failure with Fear, make no progress and the Keeper introduces an environmental complication.

**Completion:** The environment is transformed. To keep it viable, mark 1 Stress per day of fictional time. If you do not pay maintenance for three consecutive days, the environment begins to revert, a process that takes several weeks.

Create a specialized Biosphere Zone with a 1-kilometer radius. Define the ecosystem's purpose with the Keeper before beginning: agricultural, medicinal, or bio-industrial.

**Progress:** During each active session, make an Instinct roll against DC 15. On a success, advance 1 segment. On a Success with Hope, advance 2 segments.

**Completion:** Once per week of fictional time, the Zone produces Wealth Tier 3 Assets such as rare resources or medicine. Maintenance costs 1 Stress per week.

On a Success with Hope on the project's final roll, the Zone becomes self-sustaining and requires no weekly maintenance while it remains free of major external disruption.

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You transform your physical form for 1 hour into any non-unique creature of a similar size (Threat Level 2 or lower). You gain one of its key physical Ancestry Gifts or creature features. Failure: You are stuck in a random, awkward hybrid form for 1d6 hours (Disadvantage on all rolls).

*Once per session*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope + 1 Stress. For one scene, transform into a living weapon. Choose two: • Bone Shards: Ranged attack (Far), (Proficiency)×d12 physical dmg. • Carapace Plating: gain 2 temporary Armor Slots and Resistance to Physical damage. • Toxin Glands: Unarmed attacks inflict Toxin (target is Weakened; Strength Reaction Roll (DC 15) ends). Failure: Unstable shift. You are stuck in a painful hybrid form for 1d4 rounds, suffering Disadvantage on all rolls.

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You merge the consciousness of up to 6 willing creatures for one scene. All targets gain Advantage on all rolls for the duration and share a pool of 1d6 temporary HP. Cost: 3 Hope + 2 Stress. Failure: The merging is jarring. All targets suffer Trauma (Disadvantage on rolls using their lowest Trait) for 1d6 hours.

Design a custom plague or biological weapon as a Tier 5 Artifact. Before beginning, define its transmission vectors, target organisms, specific effects, and possible cure or neutralization methods with the Keeper.

**Progress:** During each Downtime phase devoted to the project, make a Knowledge roll against DC 20. On a success, advance 1 segment.

**Completion:** The biological weapon exists and functions according to the agreed parameters.

On a failure on the project's final roll, you contract a permanent biological vulnerability. You have Disadvantage on all rolls against disease and toxins until a specialized medical practitioner—such as an Engineer with Medical Technician Mastery—treats you over the course of a full story arc.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Connect all willing organic life in a Planetary/Sector size for 1 month. Damage is shared and distributed evenly. Cost: 1 HP per day from each participant. Failure: Biological chaos deals 1d6 physical damage to all connected individuals.
cost: 3 Hope + 1 HP per participant per day

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). This is a Long-Term Project (8-clock) to create 1 sentient creature (Threat Level 4) or 1d4 non-sentient (Threat Level 2) loyal

to you. Failure: The creature is unstable and hostile, attacking immediately.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 4 Hope. For one round, all allied characters gain Advantage on all rolls and recover 1 Stress and 1 HP. All adversaries suffer Disadvantage on all rolls. Failure: A system-wide biological shutdown requires you to reduce your max Stress by 1 for 1d4 days.

Mythic. Once per campaign. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 30). For 1 year, all willing life forms (biological, tech, cosmic) in a star system gain +1 to their Instinct and Knowledge Traits. Cost: 5 Hope + 5 Stress. Failure: You suffer Disadvantage on all rolls for 1d6 days and permanently lose 1 HP.

Mythic. Once per session. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 5 Hope. Instantly heal to full HP OR inflict 4d12 Void damage (ignoring armor/defenses) to one target in Very Far range. Failure: The effect is reversed. You take 4d12 damage and the Keeper gains 4 Fear tokens.
Spend 1 Hope. For one scene, you can instantly understand and speak any language, including non-verbal idioms. You gain Advantage on social rolls where cultural context is key.

Spend 1 Hope. For 1 hour, you create a perfect disguise matching any person you have observed. You gain Advantage on Presence rolls to maintain the deception. It is flawless to casual observation but can be seen through with a DC 15 Instinct check on close scrutiny.
Spend 1 Hope when making a Presence roll to persuade, deceive, or convince. You may add your Tier (1-4) to the roll. Treat any Hope die result of 11 as a 12.

Mark 1 Stress. Choose a target in Close range and make a contested Presence vs. Instinct roll. Success: You shift their emotional state for 10 minutes (calm anger, inspire fear, instill doubt), gaining Advantage on social rolls against them for the duration.

Mark 1 Stress. All allies in Close range gain a +2 bonus to their next roll and Advantage against fear or despair effects for 10 minutes. In combat, this grants a +1 bonus to their next attack roll instead.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15) vs. target's Presence+Instinct. Success: You convince them to take one specific, non-harmful action that seems reasonable to them. Lasts 1 hour. Failure: The target becomes suspicious, and the Keeper gains 1 Fear token.

Cost: 1 Hope. Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You create a perfect disguise that can fool even close friends/family for 24 hours. On a Success with Hope: You gain one piece of the target's personal experience, which you can share to prove your identity. Failure: The disguise has obvious flaws; targets gain Advantage to see through it.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). All allies in Close range immediately gain temporary HP equal to your Presence Trait, gain +2 to all rolls for 1 round, and are immune to fear/despair for the scene. On a Success with Hope: You also heal 1 Stress from each affected ally.

Cost: 1 Hope. Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You create an elaborate deception involving up to 10 willing or unaware people for 24 hours. On a Success with Hope: Participants act as if the deception is reality, suffering Disadvantage on any Instinct checks made to discern the truth.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You create or alter a reputation for yourself across a star system for 1 month. You gain +2 Reputation with a chosen faction. On a Success with Hope: The effect becomes permanent as long as you spend 1 Stress per week to maintain it (a Downtime activity).

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20) vs. target's Presence+Instinct. Success: You subtly manipulate the target's social relationships for 1 week (sowing discord, forging alliances). Failure: The target immediately detects the manipulation, gaining Advantage on all rolls against you for 1 week.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You gain recognized authority over a community/organization (Threat Level 4 or lower) for 1 month. On a Success with Hope: Your authority becomes permanent as long as you spend 1 Stress per week to maintain it (a Downtime activity).

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You convince a large group (up to 100 people) to believe a specific, significant lie for 1 week. Failure: The lie backfires, causing a chaotic response; the Keeper gains 2 Fear tokens.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 3 Hope + 3 Stress. Erase one person, event, or data point from a system's public consciousness. Affects records and memories of those not directly involved. Failure: The concept goes viral. Your involvement is revealed (-2 Reputation with the dominant faction).

*Once per session*

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You completely assume someone's identity for one scene, gaining access to their social position and resources. Failure: Your original identity surfaces, and the target organization becomes permanently Distrustful (-1 RP).

Inspire a devoted group of followers in a region or faction. Treat the group as Threat Level 3 and loyal. Define the cult's nature and limitations with the Keeper before beginning.

**Progress:** During each active work session, make a Presence roll against DC 20. On a success, advance 1 segment. On a Success with Hope, advance 2 segments.

**Completion:** The group exists and remains loyal. Maintenance costs 1 Stress per week of fictional time.

On a failure on the project's final roll, or if maintenance is unpaid for two consecutive weeks, the population becomes violently hostile toward you and you lose 2 RP with the local faction.

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You plant a compelling, immediate idea that spreads virally through a population (max 10,000) for one scene. Affected NPCs act toward an objective you choose. Failure: The idea mutates, causing paranoia and hostility toward you.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). You permanently increase or decrease your Reputation by 2 with any two major factions. Requires a full Downtime session of political work. Failure: You are caught in the middle, decreasing your Reputation by 3 with both factions.

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You create a localized social reality in a 1km radius for one scene (e.g., target believes you are the Supreme Commander). On a Success with Hope: The effect is believed by anyone viewing remotely. Failure: You suffer Disadvantage on all Presence and social rolls for 1d6 days as your reputation becomes tainted by the failed deception.

Mythic. Once per campaign. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Permanently establish a new Faction (Tier 5 Asset) with +2 RP with one major faction. Cost: Requires 5 Hope and 5 Stress. Failure: The new faction is crippled by internal strife; the Keeper gains 6 Fear tokens.

Mythic. Once per campaign. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Immediately broker a lasting non-aggression pact between two rival Great Houses. Cost: Requires 5 Hope and 5 Stress. Failure: The attempt backfires, resulting in an immediate Act of War (-5 RP) against you from one of the factions.
Reaction. When targeted by a mental effect or Neural damage, you may Mark 1 Stress. Reduce incoming Neural damage by (Proficiency)×d6 and gain Advantage on any roll to resist the effect.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 10). For 1 minute, you extend your psychic awareness into a single object within Far range, treating it as an extension of your own kinesthetic sense. You can move it with the precision of your own hands (up to 50 lbs), manipulating controls, retrieving items,

weaving it through obstacles. As an action, you can hurl the tethered object at a target to deal (Proficiency)×d6 Void damage; the impact carries the force of focused will, not muscle.
Spend 1 Hope. For one scene, you sense the surface emotions and thoughts of creatures within Close range. You gain Advantage on Instinct checks to detect lies and hostile intent.

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15) while touching an object or location. You experience a vivid impression of the most emotionally significant event that occurred there within the last week. On a Success with Hope: You can see events up to a month old and gain Advantage on your next roll related to the information.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15) targeting a creature within Close range. Success: The target is Dazed (Disadvantage on Knowledge/Instinct rolls) until the end of its next turn. On a Success with Hope: The target is Stunned for 1 round instead.
Spend 1 Hope. Create a mental link with all willing allies in Far range for one scene. You share surface thoughts and feelings. When one member spends Hope, all others gain +1 to their next roll.

Cost: 1 Hope. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You impose your will on the motor cortex of one target within Close range. Choose one, Compel: The target takes a single involuntary step in any direction up to Far range; their body obeys you before they can resist. Stagger: The target falls Prone as their balance briefly fails them, neural confusion, not physical force. Field of Hesitation: Choose a small area within Close range; for one scene, any creature attempting to cross it must succeed on a Presence check (DC 10) or lose their action to a wave of psychic indecision. This functions as Tier 1 Cover against creatures who fail.

Cost: 1 Stress. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You weave a zone of compelled stillness across a path, doorway, or threshold within Close range. Any creature attempting to cross must succeed on a Presence check (DC 15 + your Knowledge modifier) or find their will overridden, they cannot proceed and are Dazed until the start of their next turn. The Cordon itself has 10 effective HP; Neural damage dissolves it normally, while physical attacks pass straight through (the barrier exists in mind-space, not matter). A determined hostile may bypass the Cordon by spending 1 Stress as a free action, willpower breaks before the body. You can move the Cordon up to your speed as an action.

Reaction. When an adversary in Close range deals damage to you, Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Success: They take (Proficiency)×d8 Void damage and must pass a DC 15 Instinct check or become Vulnerable until the end of their next turn.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20) against a creature in Far range. Success: Deal (Proficiency)×d12 Void damage ignoring armor. The target must make a DC 15 Presence check or be Stunned until the end of its next turn.

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Cost: 2 Hope. You gain a brief vision of one likely outcome. For your next turn only, you may use this vision to either gain Advantage on one roll OR force an enemy to reroll an attack against you.
Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope. You link the minds of up to 6 willing creatures in Far range for one scene. You share thoughts, senses, and experiences instantly across any distance.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20) targeting all adversaries in Close range. Success: Assault them with psychic energy, dealing (Proficiency)×d10 Void damage. They must pass a DC 15 Presence check or Mark 1 Stress.

Cost: 2 Hope + 1 Stress. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You raise a lattice of disciplined thought around yourself and your allies, sealing every mind in the area against intrusion. For one scene, you and all allies in Close range are immune to mental, social, and emotional manipulation effects (charm, fear, deception, intimidation, psychic intrusion, compulsion). Once during the scene, when an enemy would target you or an ally with such an effect, you may reflect the attempt back at its caster: they make the contested roll against themselves at Disadvantage. Failure: The lattice forms inverted. You and all allies in Close range have Disadvantage on Presence and Instinct rolls until the end of the scene; the Keeper gains 2 Fear.

*Once per session*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 3 Hope + 1 Stress. You stabilize physics in a Very Far range area for one scene. All Void, Ethereal, and Precursor effects have Disadvantage on rolls within the area. Failure: The sudden stabilization causes a shockwave, dealing 1 Stress to all allies.

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Target one creature in Very Far range. Deal 3d8 Void damage ignoring armor. The target suffers Disadvantage on all rolls for 1 round. Failure: The damage rebounds, dealing 1d8 Void damage to you.

Mark 2 Stress and Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Create a reality distortion in Close range for one scene. All creatures in the area (including you) have Disadvantage on all rolls. Failure: You are immediately subjected to the Veil Storm effects until you clear 2 Stress.

Mark 3 Stress. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Force a complete reroll on any one roll you witness. You may modify the result by +3 or -3. Failure: You must apply the worst possible result to the roll and take 2 Stress.

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Affects all adversaries in Far range. Deal 3d6 Void damage. Targets make a DC 15 Instinct check or become Stunned for 1 round and Vulnerable for the scene. Cost: 5 Hope + 2 Stress. Failure: You are overwhelmed (Disadvantage on all rolls) for 1d4 rounds.

Mythic. Once per long rest. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Share consciousness with a willing target across a planetary system for one scene. You can both use each other's Abilities, Domain powers, and Traits. Failure: Minds clash, reducing the Instinct or Presence Trait of both targets by 1 until the next long rest.

*Once per session [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per session. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Base cost: 3 Hope + 1 Stress. You synchronize with the quantum field, briefly becoming the field itself. Choose one foundational mode: Rewind: Undo the last Keeper turn. Restore 1 Hope and clear 1 Stress to each ally who was affected by it. Accelerate: Until the end of the next round, all allies gain 1 extra action on their turn. Restructure: Move all creatures and unattended objects within Far range up to your speed in any direction; this is not forced movement for combat purposes, bodies simply find themselves elsewhere. Deepening, Dream-Project (premium mode): Instead of a foundational mode, channel a sustained dreamform. Pay an additional 2 Hope + 1 Stress to enter the base illusion: up to 3 targets within Far range are caught in a shared psychic illusion lasting one scene; each cannot perceive baseline reality unless they succeed on a DC 15 Instinct check (re-attempt at the start of each of their turns). Allies caught in the area may opt-in to Lucid mode and act normally within the dream-construct. You may invest further at the moment of casting: +1 Hope adds 1 additional target (max 6) OR raises the escape DC one rung on the standard ladder, to a ceiling of DC 20; +1 Stress (paid alongside Hope investment) extends the duration to until the next Long Rest instead of one scene. Maximum total investment: 6 Hope + 3 Stress for 6 targets at DC 20 lasting until Long Rest. Failure: The effect inverts. Adversaries within Far range receive the chosen mode's benefit; you mark 4 Stress. If the chosen mode was Dream-Project, you are also Stunned for 1 round and have Disadvantage on Presence and Instinct rolls for the rest of the scene.

## KINETIC DOMAIN

*Card label `KINETIC`. The crimson banner. Kinetic Powers are the control over kinetic force. This is the domain of unstoppable impacts and immovable objects. Practitioners create barriers of pure force, improve their own speed to impossible levels, strike with the concussive power of a meteor.*

Reaction. When you or an ally in Very Close range is hit by an attack, you may Spend 1 Hope to create a kinetic barrier. You provide +3 Evasion against that attack. If the attack misses due to this bonus, the attacker takes (Proficiency)×d4 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag.

Spend 1 Hope when making a melee attack. Hit: Deal Weapon Damage + Kinetic Trait + 1d8 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag. Empower: You may spend up to 2 additional Hope (3 Hope total) at the moment of the strike. For each additional Hope spent, add 1 die of (Proficiency)d6 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag. Ballistic Impact: If total damage triggers Overkill (exceeds Major Threshold +10), target is Pushed Short distance. If they collide with a solid object, they are knocked Prone.

Reaction. When an ally in Close range is targeted by an attack, you may Spend 1 Hope. They gain Advantage on

their defense and 2 temporary Armor Slots until the start of your next turn.

Reaction. When taking physical damage, you may Mark 1 Stress. Reduce the incoming damage by (Proficiency)×d6+2. On your next turn, you can add the absorbed amount to one attack's damage or gain +2 movement speed.

## HOW TO BUILD A LOADOUT

A practical note for players: by the end of Tier 3, an Awakened character may have access to 15+ Powers in their Vault. The **Loadout cap** (Chapter 18) determines how many they can carry into a session: 5 cards at Tier 1, 6 at Tier 2, and 7 at Tier 3, regardless of class.

The art of Loadout-building is **scene-anticipation**: thinking about what kind of work this session is likely to demand, and equipping accordingly. A combat-heavy session deserves combat-aligned Powers; a negotiation deserves Social and Lux. Most experienced players carry a mix, two combat-utility, two scene-shaping, one signature, and revise per session as the campaign clarifies.

Some Powers are good for almost every session and tend to live permanently in the Loadout (the Engineer's *Quantum Firewall*, the Mystic's *Mind Shield*, the Diplomat's *Silver Tongue*). Others are situational and earn their slot when the situation arrives.

**Recall Costs** (RC) matter. Powers with RC 0-1 swap freely mid-scene; RC 2-3 Powers commit you to that loadout for the encounter. Build with that in mind: keep your high-RC powers as known commitments, your low-RC powers as flexible response.

The *catalog* in this chapter is the resource. The *Loadout* is the choice. Build deliberately. The campaign will reward foresight; it will not reward over-preparation. Bring what you can use; leave what you cannot.

## CLOSING: THE CATALOG IS NOT THE PRACTICE

The Powers here are the system's content, not the practice of being Awakened; that practice is in the choosing, the cost, and what each Power says about who your character is becoming. The catalog is the starting place. The character is what you build from it. Welcome to the practice.
